m3l4.question: Bitcoin's fixed 21M supply provides which macro benefit?

choices.text: A non-inflatable monetary anchor
Guaranteed economic growth
Automatic full employment
Elimination of business cycles

m3l5.question: The IMF has historically expressed concern about Bitcoin adoption because of:

choices.text: Risks to financial stability and monetary sovereignty
Excessive support for IMF program countries
Reduced demand for SDR allocations
Improvements in tax compliance

m3l5.question: The phrase "inflection point" in this lesson refers to:

choices.text: A structural shift from fiat-dominated to multi-asset reserve regimes
A change in Bitcoin's block reward schedule
The launch of Bitcoin's lightning network
A specific date set by the Federal Reserve

m1l1.question: According to the lesson, what is the most common — and incorrect — message victims of crypto fraud are receiving from local law enforcement?

choices.text: That law enforcement cannot investigate cryptocurrency-related crimes
That they should hire a private investigator within 24 hours
That crypto crimes are automatically prosecuted by the SEC
That they need to convert any remaining funds to cash immediately

m1l1.question: What is the first practical step a department can take to begin properly addressing cryptocurrency crime?

choices.text: Buy commercial blockchain analytics software immediately
Add unique RMS codes or sub-codes for cryptocurrency-related offenses
Hire a full-time blockchain forensic analyst
Refer all cases to the FBI without investigation

m1l1.question: Why does the lesson criticize many of the "crypto for cops" courses currently on the market?

choices.text: They are too long and too academic for working investigators
They focus only on Ethereum and ignore Bitcoin
They skip the technical foundation and jump to visual tracing and seizure
They are only available to federal agents

m1l1.question: What is the goal of this Foundations module by the time you finish it?

choices.text: To make you a certified blockchain forensic analyst
To give you the language and conceptual scaffolding before deeper modules
To prepare you to write subpoenas to foreign exchanges
To teach you to operate a Bitcoin mining rig
Issues all U.S. dollar bills and coins
Acts as the U.S. financial intelligence unit, collecting and analyzing SARs
Operates the Bitcoin network on behalf of the Treasury
Licenses every cryptocurrency exchange operating in the U.S.

m1l2.question: A "SAR" is a Suspicious Activity Report. Who files it, and where does it go?

choices.text: A victim files it with their local police
A financial institution files it with FinCEN
A judge files it with the AUSA
An exchange files it directly with the FBI

m1l2.question: What is the role of OFAC in cryptocurrency investigations?

choices.text: It issues mining licenses to U.S. companies
It enforces U.S. sanctions, including sanctions on specific crypto addresses
It runs the public Bitcoin blockchain in North America
It sets the tax rate on cryptocurrency capital gains

m1l2.question: A "VASP" — Virtual Asset Service Provider — refers to:

choices.text: Any individual who personally owns cryptocurrency
A government employee assigned to a crypto task force
A business that handles crypto on behalf of customers (e.g., exchange, custodian)
A type of hardware wallet manufactured in Switzerland

m1l2.question: An MLAT is the formal mechanism for:

choices.text: Multi-Layer Asset Tracing through blockchain explorers
Getting evidence from a foreign country through treaty processes
Mandating Local Agency Training in cryptocurrency
Mining Liquidity Across Tokens during seizure

m1l3.question: In the financial-crime triad, what is the primary role of a Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) like FinCEN?

choices.text: To arrest suspects identified by exchanges
To collect and analyze suspicious activity reports and disseminate findings
To prosecute money laundering cases in federal court
To set interest rates for U.S. commercial banks

m1l3.question: Which agency is a regulator (not a law enforcement agency) in this framework?

choices.text: FBI
HSI
SEC
IRS Criminal Investigation

m1l3.question: When an exchange is fined hundreds of millions of dollars for poor KYC practices, that is typically:

choices.text: A regulator action, not a criminal prosecution
A SAR from FinCEN
A criminal indictment by the AUSA
A civil suit brought by victims

m1l3.question: Why is the reclassification of crypto crimes as "financial crimes" rather than "cybercrime" important to local investigators?

choices.text: It removes any need for technical evidence
It brings crypto cases under existing BSA/AML/SAR frameworks with established intelligence pipes
It transfers all jurisdiction to the SEC
It eliminates the need for federal partners on local cases

m1l4.question: What is the defining feature of a "centralized" digital asset?

choices.text: It can be sent across international borders without restriction
It is managed, issued, and regulated by a single entity that controls creation and records
It uses cryptography to secure transactions
It has a fixed maximum supply that cannot be increased

m1l4.question: Which of the following is an example of a decentralized digital asset?

choices.text: Marriott Bonvoy hotel points
A Visa credit card balance
Bitcoin
Fortnite V-Bucks

m1l4.question: A victim reports their funds were drained from MetaMask. What does this tell you about the investigation path compared to funds taken from Coinbase?

choices.text: There is no difference; the path is identical
MetaMask can be subpoenaed for the user's account history just like Coinbase
MetaMask is self-custody, so the only records are on the public blockchain — no central database to subpoena
MetaMask transactions are private and cannot be traced at all

m1l4.question: What is the key compliance difference between a centralized exchange (CEX) and a decentralized exchange (DEX)?

choices.text: CEXs hold custody and follow KYC; DEXs hold no custody and have no users to identify
CEXs are illegal in the U.S.; DEXs are licensed by FinCEN
DEXs are required to file SARs; CEXs are exempt
There is no difference — both must comply with the same rules

m1l5.question: What is a "node" in a decentralized network?

choices.text: A central server that controls all transactions
A government regulator that approves cryptocurrency activity
An independent computer that runs the network software and maintains a copy of the records
A specific type of Bitcoin wallet sold by exchanges

m1l5.question: In Proof of Work, what makes cheating the Bitcoin network economically irrational?

choices.text: A government task force monitors all transactions in real time
An attacker would need to control more than half of all computing power on the network
Cheaters are automatically banned by Bitcoin's board of directors
The Bitcoin software refuses to run on cheating computers

m1l5.question: Which is the biggest consequence of decentralization for an investigator?

choices.text: Records are public and permanent, but there is no one to call to reverse a transaction
All transactions are encrypted and impossible to view
Records are deleted automatically every six months
Only certified law enforcement can read the blockchain

m1l5.question: Why does the lesson say decentralization is good news for investigators in practice?

choices.text: Because all blockchain users must register with FinCEN
Because the entry and exit choke points (exchanges, payment processors) are centralized and respond to legal process
Because cryptocurrency is rarely used for actual crimes
Because every blockchain transaction includes the user's real name

m1l6.question: A blockchain is best described as:

choices.text: A private database controlled by a single company
A public ledger of transactions organized into blocks chained in chronological order
An encryption algorithm used only by banks
A type of cryptocurrency wallet

m1l6.question: When a wallet signs a transaction, what is it proving?

choices.text: That the transaction was approved by FinCEN
That the sender authorized it, without revealing the private key itself
That the receiver has identified themselves with KYC
That the transaction is below the $10,000 reporting threshold

m1l6.question: What is the relationship between a public key and a private key in cryptocurrency?

choices.text: They are the same key used in two different ways
The private key is shared and the public key is secret
Anyone with the public key can derive the private key
The public key is shared; the private key is secret and proves control. The math is one-way.

m1l6.question: For a Bitcoin transaction, what can the blockchain prove on its own — and what can it NOT prove?

choices.text: It can prove the amount, time, and immutability — but not who the addresses belong to
It can prove the identities of both parties but not the amount
It can prove nothing without an exchange's assistance
It can prove everything including the real names of the parties

m1l7.question: What does a cryptocurrency wallet actually store?

choices.text: The cryptocurrency itself, in encrypted form
A copy of the entire blockchain
The private keys needed to authorize spending from particular addresses
The user's government-issued ID and KYC documents

m1l7.question: A 12- or 24-word seed phrase is best described as:

choices.text: A backup that regenerates the entire wallet — anyone who has it controls the funds
A password that only works on the original device
A list of approved transaction types for the wallet
The wallet's version number

m1l7.question: What is the main difference between a hot wallet and a cold wallet?

choices.text: Hot wallets are for Bitcoin only; cold wallets are for Ethereum only
Hot wallets are connected to the internet; cold wallets are not
Hot wallets cost money; cold wallets are free
Cold wallets are illegal in some U.S. states

m1l7.question: A victim says her funds are in a Coinbase account. What kind of wallet is that, and what does it mean for your investigation?

choices.text: Self-custody — only the user can recover the funds
Cold wallet — you must physically locate a hardware device
Custodial — Coinbase holds the keys; subpoena Coinbase for records
Paper wallet — the user must produce a written seed phrase

m1l7.question: The string "bc1qmyatmz67pnm8radfjpwllpl5fw4tr2cqv47zzc" is an example of:

choices.text: A private key
A seed phrase
A Bitcoin address
A wallet password

m1l8.question: What is the practical meaning of "Not your keys, not your crypto"?

choices.text: Cryptocurrency is illegal without a government-issued license
Unless you control the private keys, you do not truly own or control the asset
Only certified investigators can seize cryptocurrency
Hot wallets are always safer than cold wallets

m1l8.question: In a CUSTODIAL case (funds on a centralized exchange), the primary investigative path is:

choices.text: Search the suspect's home for a hardware wallet
Send legal process (subpoena, warrant) to the platform that holds the keys
Wait for the suspect to voluntarily transfer the funds
File a SAR with FinCEN and close the case

m1l8.question: In a SELF-CUSTODY case, the primary investigative path is:

choices.text: Subpoena the blockchain itself
Recover the keys — search the device, find the seed phrase, or compel cooperation
Issue a recall transaction on the network
Contact the wallet software vendor and ask them to freeze the account

m1l8.question: Your department seizes a suspect's laptop containing a MetaMask wallet with $200,000 in tokens. Have you seized the funds?

choices.text: Yes — possession of the laptop is possession of the funds
Yes — but only after notifying MetaMask
No — you have seized a key-storage device. To control the funds you must move them to a wallet your department controls
Only if the laptop was powered on at the time of seizure

m1l8.question: Mt. Gox and FTX are cited as cautionary tales about which kind of risk?

choices.text: The risk of using cold wallets
The risk of trusting custodial platforms with your private keys
The risk of losing your seed phrase
The risk of using Bitcoin instead of a privacy coin

m1l9.question: What is a "cross-chain bridge" and why does it complicate investigations?

choices.text: A physical bridge where bitcoin miners meet — irrelevant to investigations
A protocol that lets value move between blockchains, breaking single-chain tracing tools
A type of search warrant used in international cases
A new feature of Coinbase that prevents fraud

m1l9.question: Why is the MLAT process often a poor primary tool for crypto investigations?

choices.text: It is illegal under FinCEN regulations
It only works for cash transactions
It can take years to produce results, even where the treaty exists
MLATs are not allowed for cases under $1 million

m1l9.question: Which of the following is a true privacy coin that is particularly difficult to trace?

choices.text: USDC
Bitcoin
Ethereum
Monero

m1l9.question: According to the lesson, what makes the resource gap inside law enforcement so significant?

choices.text: Federal certifications are widely held at every state agency
Forensic tools are free and easy to obtain for all departments
Most local departments lack specialized certifications, and analytics tools are expensive
Private vendors will not work with law enforcement at any price

m1l9.question: What is the lesson's overall message about these challenges?

choices.text: They are all unsolvable; investigators should refer crypto cases to the FBI without working them
They are real but not absolute — successful case law and improving tools are paving the path
They were exaggerated; cryptocurrency cases are easy to investigate
They only apply to international cases; local crypto cases have no challenges
